thread:
Maya (Arch): Quick sync — proposing we extract session-affinity from the router into a tiny stateful service + per-pool observability sidecar. Decouples hot-path KV from routing and gives us targeted metrics.
Sam (Runtime): curious on failure modes. do we keep sticky fallback in router or always proxy to stateful? :thinking:
Maya (Arch): plan A: router proxies if a session key exists; if the service is down, router falls back to hashed-routing with a short TTL. Plan B: router retains a minimal sticky cache for 30s to cover transient outages.
Leo (SRE): prefer Plan B. fewer cross-service calls during partial outage. But it's more state in router.
Anya (Infra): we'll need clear ownership of state persistence. Are we using Redis/consensus for the session service or local ephemeral per-pool with replication?
Maya (Arch): lean ephemeral per-pool with async replication (raft-lite). durability not required beyond a few minutes. writes are mostly idempotent.
Sam (Runtime): implications for KV cache invalidation? we'll need a reconciliation loop to reconcile router cache, session service, and model runtime KV caches.
Maya (Arch): yes — reconciliation: 1) session TTL; 2) periodic snapshot checks; 3) on-miss, router asks service and updates local cache.
Leo (SRE): observability sidecar idea looks good. we can instrument per-session tail latency, request fanout, sticky-miss rate. Let's list metrics to watch in canary.
Maya (Arch): suggested canary metrics: [sticky-hit-rate, sticky-fallback-rate, p95-latency, cross-pool-requests, error-rate]. Keep 2-week baseline.
Anya (Infra): deployment surface: hosted and dedicated pools will get sidecar by default. private deployments: we provide opt-in module. also need K8s CRD for session-service config.
Sam (Runtime): coupling concern: router and session-service API must be extremely small. proto: GetSession(node_id) -> {target_pool, token} and SetSession(...). Anything else will bite us later.
Maya (Arch): agreed. single RPC, idempotent writes, opt-in hint for affinity weight. Avoid complex query ops.
Leo (SRE): rollback plan: toggle a router flag to bypass affinity; sidecar can be drained. We should add a runtime flagguard and a kill-switch metric (affinity-disabled boolean).
Maya (Arch): canary plan: 1) deploy sidecar to 5% of pools; 2) enable router proxy for those pools; 3) monitor metrics for 48h; 4) expand to 25% if stable.
Anya (Infra): infra checklist: CRD + helm chart changes, resource requests for sidecar, RBAC for session-service, memory/ephemeral storage SLOs.
Sam (Runtime): tradeoffs: extra hop on warm paths vs better scaling of router. We'll quantify token-costs and p50/p95 delta in spike tests.
Maya (Arch): action items: @Sam run perf microbench for router+sidecar on 1000 qps and share numbers. @Leo prepare alert thresholds for canary metrics. @Anya draft CRD + helm diff.
Sam (Runtime): yep I'll run the bench tomorrow.
Leo (SRE): I'll draft alerts and a runbook snippet for affinity degradation.
Anya (Infra): I'll put together CRD + helm in a branch and tag you all.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary namespace deployment started for session-sidecar v0.1.0 :eyes:
Maya (Arch): thanks — added a short PR with interface proto skeleton to the repo. link: https://git.internal/redwood/session-affinity-proto
Sam (Runtime): quick thought — add a "best-effort-ttl" header so clients can prefer non-sticky lookups. gives us traffic steering for experiments.
Maya (Arch): good call — include "X-Affinity-Preference: best-effort|strict" in the proto and router header mapping.
Leo (SRE): final note: prioritize observability signals that let us detect split-brain for the session-service. heartbeat + leader age metric.
Maya (Arch): agreed. I'll consolidate notes into an RFC follow-up doc and a small checklist for the first rollout.
Sam (Runtime): cool. low-touch on interface, high attention on metrics. :thumbsup:
Maya (Arch): closing — will post the RFC link in #architecture when ready.
